newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB and Zennoh establish Australia-Japan grain j/v. [corrected 09:59 gmt]
newsitem.headline: AWB and Zennoh establish Australia-Japan grain j/v. [corrected 09:59 gmt]

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) and the Zennoh agricultural group of Japan had established a joint venture company in Japan to import, export, buy and market feedgrains, oilseeds and pulses, the AWB said on Tuesday.

AWB-Zennoh Ltd would build on an already strong relationship based on sorghum trading and Zennoh's purchases of wheat for compound feed manufacture, AWB managing director John Lawrenson said in a statement.
"The venture reinforces AWB's commitment to Japan and the trading of non-wheat products," he said.
"It will also assist Zennoh to maintain long-term stable supplies of grain from Australia," Lawrenson said.
The co-operation was designed to foster new feedgrain business and would not affect either AWB's or Zennoh's traditional business, he said.
Moto Motohashi, chairman of Zennoh, Japan's National Federation of Agricultural Corporations, said his organisation was very pleased about the joint-venture.
"It will be a big step in linking Australian and Japanese farmers," he said in the statement.
Zennoh is one of the most influential forces in the Japanese grain market with an annual turnover equivalent to nearly A$60 (corrects from A$100) billion, Lawrenson said.
It is a federation of agricultural co-operatives and one of the largest such organisations in the world, Lawrenson said.
The organisation serves farmers in Japan through more than 2,500 regional co-operatives and economic federations by supplying a wide range of farm inputs, including imported feedgrains.
Zennoh was an ideal partner for the AWB because it owned significant grain handling facilities in Japan for the import and distribution of grain, Lawrenson said.
It is the largest importer of feedgrains in Japan, which in turn is the largest feedgrain importing country in the world, and is the largest compound feed manufacturer in Japan, he said.
Lawrenson said the AWB did not intend to move away from its strong relationships with Japanese trading houses in the marketing of wheat to Japan.
"There will be no change in the way the AWB conducts its existing business in Japan, but this is a significant opportunity for us to be involved in new business," he said.
AWB-Zennoh Ltd is a registered joint venture company in Japan with AWB holding a 51 percent share of the new enterprise and Zennoh the remainder.
